extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators and technical contacts of public water systems (PWSs), and laboratories performing UCMR analyses
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedures for reporting, record retention, and data submission for Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Regulation (UCMR) and other Part 141 monitoring by public water systems and their laboratories. Covers timelines, methods of submission, required data elements, representative sampling, and recordkeeping durations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for routine test result reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where a shorter period is specified in this part, the supplier of water shall report to the State the results of any test measurement or analysis required by this part within (1) the first ten days following the month in which the result is received, or (2) the first ten days following the end of the required monitoring period as stipulated by the State, whichever of these is shortest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate reporting of compliance failures
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where a different reporting period is specified in this part, the supplier of water must report to the State within 48 hours the failure to comply with any national primary drinking water regulation (including failure to comply with monitoring requirements) set forth in this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: State laboratory reporting exception
rubrics_metrics.description: The supplier of water is not required to report analytical results to the State in cases where a State laboratory performs the analysis and reports the results to the State office which would normally receive such notification from the supplier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of public notification compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The public water system, within 10 days of completing the public notification requirements under subpart Q of this part for the initial public notice and any repeat notices, must submit to the primary agency a certification that it has fully complied with the public notification regulations under subpart Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification must include a representative copy of each type of notice distributed, published, posted, and made available to the persons served by the system and to the media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 1 lead action level notice to EPA/primacy
rubrics_metrics.description: For Tier 1 notices for a lead action level exceedance, public water systems must provide a copy of the Tier 1 notice to the Administrator and the head of the primacy agency as soon as practicable, but not later than 24 hours after the public water system learns of the exceedance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of records upon request
rubrics_metrics.description: The water supply system shall submit to the State within the time stated in the request copies of any records required to be maintained under § 141.33 hereof or copies of any documents then in existence which the State or the Administrator is entitled to inspect pursuant to the authority of section 1445 of the Safe Drinking Water Act or the equivalent provisions of State law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention: microbiological and turbidity analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Records of microbiological analyses and turbidity analyses made pursuant to this part shall be kept for not less than 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual laboratory reports may be kept, or data may be transferred to tabular summaries, provided that specified information (date/place/time of sampling, sampler name, sample identification, date of analysis, lab/person performing analysis, analytical technique/method used, results) is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention: chemical analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Records of chemical analyses made pursuant to this part shall be kept for not less than 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual laboratory reports may be kept, or data may be transferred to tabular summaries, provided that the required information is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of laboratory reports or summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Actual laboratory reports may be kept, or data may be transferred to tabular summaries, provided that the following information is included:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required information includes: (1) date, place, and time of sampling, and name of sampler; (2) identification of sample type (routine distribution, check, raw/process, special purpose); (3) date of analysis; (4) laboratory and person responsible for performing analysis; (5) the analytical technique/method used; and (6) the results of the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention: corrective actions for violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Records of action taken by the system to correct violations of primary drinking water regulations shall be kept for a period not less than 3 years after the last action taken with respect to the particular violation involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention: sanitary surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of any written reports, summaries or communications relating to sanitary surveys of the system conducted by the system itself, by a private consultant, or by any local, State or Federal agency, shall be kept for a period not less than 10 years after completion of the sanitary survey involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention: variance or exemption records
rubrics_metrics.description: Records concerning a variance or exemption granted to the system shall be kept for a period ending not less than 5 years following the expiration of such variance or exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention: public notices and certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of public notices issued pursuant to subpart Q of this part and certifications made to the primacy agency pursuant to § 141.31 must be kept for three years after issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention period for monitoring plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of monitoring plans developed pursuant to this part shall be kept for the same period of time as the records of analyses taken under the plan are required to be kept under paragraph (a) of this section, except as specified elsewhere in this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: UCMR applicability and key definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: This section applies to any owner or operator of a public water system required to monitor for unregulated contaminants under § 141.40(a); such owner or operator is referred to as 'you.' For purposes of this section, definitions for PWS 'population served', 'finished', 'State', 'PWS Official', and 'PWS Technical Contact' are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PWS population served is the retail population reported to SDWIS/Fed; 'finished' means water introduced into distribution intended for consumption without further treatment except necessary distribution treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to submit UCMR reporting information
rubrics_metrics.description: Some reporting requirements must be fulfilled electronically and others by mail. Information that must be submitted using EPA's electronic data reporting system must be submitted through: https://www.epa.gov/dwucmr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation required to be mailed can be submitted to the UCMR Sampling Coordinator at the EPA Technical Support Center or by email to UCMR_Sampling_Coordinator@epa.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of UCMR data and CCR inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: You must notify the public of the availability of unregulated contaminant monitoring data as provided in subpart Q. Community Water Systems that detect unregulated contaminants under this monitoring must also address such detections as part of their Consumer Confidence Reports, as provided in subpart O.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to contest UCMR applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have received a letter from EPA or your State concerning your required monitoring and your system does not meet the applicability criteria for UCMR, or if a change occurs at your system that may affect your requirements under UCMR, you must mail or email a letter to EPA as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter must be from your PWS Official, include your PWSID Code, an explanation why UCMR requirements are not applicable or have changed, and appropriate contact information; EPA will make an applicability determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large systems: required contact and zip code information
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems serving a population of more than 10,000 and meeting applicability criteria must provide contact information by December 31, 2022, and provide updates within 30 days if this information changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact information must be submitted electronically and include name, affiliation, mailing address, phone number, and email for your PWS Technical Contact and your PWS Official; also report U.S. Postal Service Zip Code(s) for all areas served as a one-time requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling location inventory submission and updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Large systems must provide inventory information by December 31, 2022, using EPA's electronic data reporting system, and must submit, verify, or update data elements 1-9 for each sampling location (or approved representative sampling location).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inventory information changes (new sources or sampling locations put in use before or during sampling), report updates to EPA's electronic system within 30 days of the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification to propose representative ground water sampling locations
rubrics_metrics.description: Large PWSs that have EPA- or State-approved representative EPTDS sampling locations from a previous UCMR cycle may submit documentation; PWSs without approval may propose representative EPTDS sampling if: you use ground water, all well sources have either the same treatment or no treatment, and you have multiple EPTDSs from the same source (same aquifer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit existing or proposed representative EPTDS plan at least six months prior to scheduled sample collection using the electronic submission method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration requirements for representative wells
rubrics_metrics.description: If proposing representative EPTDS(s), you must demonstrate that any proposed representative EPTDS is associated with a well that draws from the same aquifer as the wells it will represent and is representative of the highest annual volume and most consistently active wells in the array.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit Table 1 information for each proposed representative sampling location and include documentation such as well logs/construction drawings, data demonstrating relative homogeneity of water-quality constituents, data showing wells are located in a limited geographic area (e.g., within 0.5 mile), and hydrogeologic travel time data if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval process for representative sampling plans
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA or the State will review representative sampling proposals and coordinate necessary changes; the plan will not be final until you receive written approval from EPA identifying the final list of EPTDSs where you will be required to monitor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting EPA if not notified of UCMR requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If you believe you are subject to UCMR requirements and have not been contacted by EPA or your State by April 26, 2022, you must send a letter to EPA as specified. Letter must be from your PWS Official and must include an explanation why requirements are applicable and appropriate contact information; a copy must be submitted to the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will make an applicability determination and notify you regarding applicability status and required sampling schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescheduling monitoring (large systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Large systems may independently change their monitoring schedules up to December 31, 2022, using EPA's electronic data reporting system. After this date, if your PWS cannot sample according to your assigned schedule you must mail or email a letter to EPA prior to the scheduled sampling date including an explanation and the alternative schedule requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must not reschedule monitoring specifically to avoid sample collection during a suspected vulnerable period. You remain subject to your assigned schedule unless and until you receive a letter from EPA specifying a new schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to rescheduling notification for ground water
rubrics_metrics.description: For ground water sampling, if the second round of sampling will be completed five to seven months after the first sampling event (as specified in Table 2 of § 141.40(a)(4)(i)(B)), no notification to EPA is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any ground water sampling location will be non-operational for more than one month before and one month after the month in which the second sampling event is scheduled, you must notify EPA explaining why the schedule cannot be met and comply with any modified schedule provided by EPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting monitoring results and changes
rubrics_metrics.description: For UCMR samples, you must report all data elements specified in Table 1 of paragraph (e) using EPA's electronic data reporting system. You also must report any changes to data elements 1 through 9 to EPA in writing, explaining the nature and purpose of the proposed change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory responsibilities and PWS approval duties
rubrics_metrics.description: You are responsible for ensuring that the laboratory conducting the analysis of your unregulated contaminant monitoring samples posts the analytical results to EPA's electronic data reporting system. You are also responsible for reviewing, approving, and submitting those results to EPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting timeline for lab posting and PWS approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Require laboratory to post and approve data in EPA's electronic reporting system for your review within 90 days from the sample collection date. You then have 30 days from when the laboratory posts and approves your data to review, approve, and submit the data to the State and EPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not electronically approve and submit the laboratory data within 30 days of the laboratory posting approved data, the data will be considered approved by you and available for State and EPA review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single official result when multiple valid analyses exist
rubrics_metrics.description: If you report more than one set of valid results for the same sampling location and the same sampling event, EPA will use the highest of the reported values as the official result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include multiple labs analyzing replicate samples or multiple samples collected during a single monitoring event at the same location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using previously collected data for UCMR
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot report previously collected data to meet the testing and reporting requirements for the contaminants listed in § 141.40(a)(3). All analyses must be performed by laboratories approved by EPA to perform UCMR analyses using the analytical methods specified in Table 1 of § 141.40(a)(3) and using samples collected according to § 141.40(a)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Small system reporting: contact information and inventory
rubrics_metrics.description: If you serve a population of 10,000 or fewer and are selected for UCMR monitoring, your reporting requirements will be specified within EPA materials sent to you, including a request for contact information and sampling-kit related information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will request contact information for key individuals; provide within 90 days and update within 30 days of change. Provide sampling location inventory by Dec 31, 2022, record data elements 1-9 on sample form and bottle, send per sampling kit instructions, and report changes to data elements 1-9 by email explaining nature and purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 1: Public Water System Identification (PWSID) Code
rubrics_metrics.description: The code used to identify each PWS. The code begins with the standard 2-character postal State abbreviation or Region code; the remaining 7 numbers are unique to each PWS in the State. The same identification code must be used to represent the PWS identification for all current and future UCMR monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 2: Public Water System Name
rubrics_metrics.description: Unique name, assigned once by the PWS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 3: Public Water System Facility Identification Code
rubrics_metrics.description: An identification code established by the State or, at the State's discretion, by the PWS, following the format of a 5-digit number unique within each PWS for each applicable facility (i.e., for each source of water, treatment plant, distribution system, or any other facility associated with water treatment or delivery). The same identification code must be used to represent the facility for all current and future UCMR monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 4: Public Water System Facility Name
rubrics_metrics.description: Unique name, assigned once by the PWS, for every facility ID (e.g., Treatment Plant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 5: Public Water System Facility Type
rubrics_metrics.description: That code that identifies that type of facility as either: CC = Consecutive connection. SS = Sampling station. TP = Treatment plant. OT = Other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 6: Water Source Type
rubrics_metrics.description: The type of source water that supplies a water system facility. Systems must report one of the following codes for each sampling location: SW = Surface water; GU = Ground water under the direct influence of surface water; MX = Mixed water; GW = Ground water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting depends on the source status during the 12-month period (e.g., 'SW' reported if served entirely by a surface water source during the 12-month period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 7: Sampling Point Identification Code
rubrics_metrics.description: An identification code established by the State, or at the State's discretion, by the PWS, that uniquely identifies each sampling point. Each sampling code must be unique within each applicable facility, for each applicable sampling location (i.e., entry point to the distribution system). The same identification code must be used to represent the sampling location for all current and future UCMR monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 8: Sampling Point Name
rubrics_metrics.description: Unique sample point name, assigned once by the PWS, for every sample point ID (e.g., Entry Point).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 9: Sampling Point Type Code
rubrics_metrics.description: A code that identifies the location of the sampling point as: EP = Entry point to the distribution system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 10: Disinfectant Type
rubrics_metrics.description: All of the disinfectants/oxidants that have been added prior to and at the entry point to the distribution system.
